subject: Breakpoint pricing: clarification on marginal vs blended and commit tiers
messages:
From: Alice Jones <alice.jones@brighthealth.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brighthealth.com
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Breakpoint pricing questions for Hosted API commit tiers

Hi Dev,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and multi-region routing look promising for our use case. Procurement and finance have one sticking point before we can move to a PO: how Redwood computes discounts across breakpoints. Specifically:

- Are discounts applied on a marginal basis (each token billed at the rate for the bracket it falls into) or blended (a single effective per-token rate computed across total committed volume)?
- For example, if we commit 1.2B tokens/month with breakpoints at 500M and 2B, what would show up on our invoices?

We also want to understand the true-up and reporting cadence — will you provide monthly token consumption reports and an automated true-up if we exceed committed tiers?

Can you share an example invoice math and the preferred contract language we should expect? Attaching the draft SOW for context.

Best,
Alice
Procurement, BrightHealth

Attachments: SOW_BrightHealth_2026.pdf (stated attachment)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jones <alice.jones@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Breakpoint pricing questions for Hosted API commit tiers

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear questions and for sharing the SOW. Short answer: we can do either marginal or blended billing; we typically propose marginal billing by default because it tracks usage more transparently, but we know some customers prefer a blended invoicing option to simplify accounting. Below I’ve outlined both with a worked example and recommended contract language.

1) Proposal / breakpoints (example):
- Tier A: 0 — 500M tokens/month @ $0.00040/token
- Tier B: 500M+ — 2.0B tokens/month @ $0.00032/token
- Tier C: 2.0B+ tokens/month @ $0.00025/token

2) Marginal billing (default) — how it looks:
- If you use 1.2B tokens in a month:
  - First 500M @ $0.00040 = $200,000
  - Next 700M @ $0.00032 = $224,000
  - Total = $424,000 => Effective (blended) rate = $424,000 / 1.2B = $0.0003533/token

3) Blended (single rate) — how it looks:
- If we agreed a 1.2B committed tier and a blended per-token price is preferred, we would compute a single per-token invoice rate up front for the committed volume. Example blended rate for a 1.2B commit using the above tiers (weighted average) would be ~ $0.0003533/token (same effective result in this example), but the invoice shows: 1.2B tokens @ $0.0003533 = $424,000 — no line-item marginal segments. The difference is in presentation and accounting: marginal shows the segments, blended shows a single rate.

4) Overage / true-up mechanics:
- Monthly reporting: we provide token usage reports with daily granularity and per-route breakdowns via the Console and a monthly CSV export.
- True-up: billed monthly. If you exceed the committed tier for the month, overage will be billed at the marginal rate for the bracket in which the overage sits. We can include a cap or negotiated overage step if desired.

5) Contract language (suggested snippets):
- "Billing model: Marginal. Customer will be billed per month for actual token consumption calculated across defined breakpoints. Each token will be billed at the rate for the tier in which it falls."
- OR if blended: "Billing model: Blended. Customer will be invoiced at a single per-token rate calculated based on the committed volume for the applicable billing period."

6) Practical recommendation:
- Start with marginal billing to avoid manual reconciliations; offer blended invoicing only if your accounting team requests a single-line invoice. Marginal is easier to reconcile to actual usage and to show discounts flowing through as usage grows.

I’ve attached a worked spreadsheet (RDW_proposed-ladder_v2.xlsx) that shows the math for a few usage scenarios (0.6B, 1.2B, 2.5B). If you’re comfortable with marginal billing we can mirror the exact language in section 3.2 of the SOW.

Next steps: if you want blended invoicing, let us know and we’ll produce two contract exhibits (marginal vs blended) plus an example invoice for each. Otherwise I’ll ask Legal/Finance to prepare a PO-ready exhibit for marginal billing.

Thanks — looping Marissa for approval on the proposed rate table and Neha for procurement/legal language.

— Dev
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW_proposed-ladder_v2.xlsx (spreadsheets with calculations)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Breakpoint pricing: clarification on marginal vs blended and commit tiers

Folks — quick internal: I reviewed Dev's table. Approve marginal default for this deal with one caveat: provide a monthly blended invoice option as a courtesy (no price concession) when BrightHealth requests a single-line invoice. That avoids re-negotiating unit economics later.

For Legal: suggested clause to add under Billing (we can tweak):
"If Customer requests blended invoicing, Redwood will compute the blended per-token rate using the marginal tier schedule and apply that rate for the billing period; such blended invoicing is an invoicing convenience and does not alter the underlying marginal price schedule for audit or true-up purposes."

Also confirm: any required minimum notice for changing billing mode post-go-live? I suggest a 60-day notice if they want to switch from marginal to blended after contract signature.

Marissa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

(On a separate note: recommend we include a 10% commit discount for 12-month committed spend if they sign for 12 months; Dev, we can discuss pricing floor in the margin approval call.)
